E.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
E.q: A 29-year-old woman has normal clotting screens and bleeding with skin bruising, petechiae and mucous membrane bleeding. Which category fits?
opts: A platelet disorder
Correct. Normal screens with skin bruising, petechiae and mucosal bleeding suggest platelet disorders or mild von Willebrand disease, evaluated with platelet function and von Willebrand studies.
Factor VII deficiency
Factor VII deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time, so the screens would not be normal.
Hemophilia A
Hemophilia A prolongs the partial thromboplastin time and brings deep bleeding into joints and muscles.
Hypofibrinogenemia
Significant hypofibrinogenemia prolongs the prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time and is a factor problem, so the screens would not be normal with bruising and mucosal bleeding.

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
E.q: Which of these is a provider-determined reason to end an exercise stress test?
opts: Exertional hypotension
Correct. A fall in systolic pressure below the resting standing value is a provider-determined endpoint, alongside extreme pressures, a patient who looks unwell and dangerous rhythms.
The patient wanting to stop
That is a patient-determined endpoint, in the same group as chest discomfort, severe dyspnea and fatigue, rather than a provider-determined one.
Leg cramps or joint discomfort
Cramps and joint discomfort are other limiting symptoms reported by the patient, so they are patient-determined rather than provider-determined endpoints.
A workload target set in advance
A predetermined workload or heart rate is a protocol-determined endpoint used in submaximal tests, not one the provider decides during the test.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 36

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac CT
E.q: Why is cardiac computed tomography synchronized with an electrocardiogram?
opts: To slow the heart during the scan
Slowing the heart is done with medication such as metoprolol; the electrocardiogram synchronizes the scan to the cardiac cycle but does not slow the rate.
To view different stages of the cardiac cycle
Correct. Because the heart is constantly moving, tying the scan to the tracing lets the heart be evaluated at chosen points in the cycle.
To provoke ischemia while images are taken
Provoking ischemia is the purpose of stress testing; the scan is synchronized to the tracing so the heart is imaged at set points of its cycle.
To locate the origin of an arrhythmia
Locating an arrhythmia is the work of electrophysiological testing; here the tracing only times the scan to the stages of the cardiac cycle.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 41

E.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
E.q: A 66-year-old woman takes warfarin, and her international normalized ratio is 4.8 (goal 2.0 to 3.0). What is the concern?
opts: Clot risk
A low international normalized ratio on warfarin signals clot risk. This value is above goal.
Bleeding risk
Correct. On warfarin a high international normalized ratio means over-anticoagulation and a risk of bleeding.
Platelet excess
The international normalized ratio standardizes the prothrombin time and does not assess platelet number.
Fibrinolysis
Fibrinolysis is evaluated by D-dimer, not the international normalized ratio.

E.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
E.q: A 45-year-old woman has an isolated prolonged partial thromboplastin time that does not correct when mixed one to one with normal plasma. What does this suggest?
opts: Factor VIII deficiency
A true factor deficiency corrects because normal plasma supplies the missing factor.
Factor IX deficiency
A factor IX deficiency also corrects with normal plasma, so it does not explain failure to correct.
An inhibitor
Correct. When a mixing study does not correct, an inhibitor is present, such as a specific factor inhibitor or lupus anticoagulant.
Vitamin K deficiency
Vitamin K deficiency is a factor deficiency and would correct, and it mainly prolongs the prothrombin time.

E.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
E.q: A 59-year-old man with severe malabsorption has a prolonged prothrombin time. Which liver-made protein, dependent on vitamin K, explains this?
opts: Fibrin
Fibrin is the clot formed from fibrinogen. It is not the vitamin K dependent liver protein behind this result.
Prothrombin
Correct. Prothrombin is produced by the liver and depends on vitamin K intake and absorption, so vitamin K deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time.
Plasmin
Plasmin degrades fibrin and is not the protein whose production depends on vitamin K.
von Willebrand factor
von Willebrand factor tethers platelets in primary hemostasis. It is not the vitamin K dependent protein that the prothrombin time depends on.

E.io: Analyze a lipid profile
E.q: A 61-year-old has a low HDL-C (high-density lipoprotein cholesterol), below her lab's reference limit. How is that value used?
opts: As the main target of therapy
Therapy targets LDL-C (low-density lipoprotein cholesterol) and the atherogenic particles, not HDL-C.
As proof of familial disease
Familial hypercholesterolemia is suggested by a very high LDL-C or total cholesterol, not by a low HDL-C.
As a value to ignore
It still carries risk information; it is simply not the target of treatment.
As a marker, not a target
Correct. Higher HDL-C is generally favorable, but low HDL-C is a marker, not a therapeutic goal; treatment is aimed at the apoB (apolipoprotein B) particles.

E.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
E.q: A laboratory runs a prothrombin time on a 49-year-old woman. What is added to her plasma to start the clot?
opts: A phospholipid activator
A phospholipid activator is added in the activated partial thromboplastin time to start the intrinsic pathway.
Plasmin
Plasmin degrades fibrin and would dissolve a clot. It is not used to start one.
Tissue factor
Correct. The prothrombin time is the time for a fibrin clot to form in a lab tube when tissue factor is added to the patient's plasma.
Collagen
Collagen is used to provoke platelet aggregation in function testing, not the coagulation-based prothrombin time.

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of cardiac MRI
E.q: What does cardiovascular magnetic resonance avoid that computed tomography does not?
opts: Both ionizing radiation and iodinated contrast
Correct. Both avoided at once, which matters most in the young patient and in the patient with impaired kidneys.
Dependence on the operator
Operator dependence is a limitation of ultrasound rather than the point of comparison here.
Any need for a resting heart rate
Rate control is a computed tomography requirement; it is not what magnetic resonance is described as avoiding.
Sedation and airway monitoring
Sedation is required for transesophageal echocardiography rather than being the contrast drawn here.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 55

E.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
E.q: A 52-year-old man has a prolonged partial thromboplastin time and a normal platelet count. Which phase of hemostasis is most likely affected?
opts: Primary hemostasis
Primary hemostasis is the platelet plug, evaluated by the count, smear and function tests. A prolonged partial thromboplastin time does not test it.
Fibrinolysis
Fibrinolysis is evaluated by breakdown-product tests such as D-dimer, not by the partial thromboplastin time.
Vasoconstriction
Vasoconstriction is not measured by a clotting time. A prolonged partial thromboplastin time reflects clotting factors.
Secondary hemostasis
Correct. The partial thromboplastin time tests the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways, so a prolonged result points to the clotting factors, secondary hemostasis.

E.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
E.q: What characterizes phase 1, early repolarization?
opts: Calcium channels open, producing contraction
Calcium entry and contraction belong to phase two, the plateau, rather than to early repolarization.
Sodium channels close and potassium channels reopen
Correct. The inward current stops and an outward one resumes, which begins bringing the membrane back down.
Fast sodium channels open
Sodium channel opening is phase zero; in phase one they close.
The membrane returns fully to minus ninety millivolts
The full return to resting voltage is completed in phase three rather than phase one.

E.io: Compare and contrast cardiac biomarkers: Creatine kinase, Cardiac troponins, BNP, hs-CRP
E.q: A 58-year-old is evaluated for exertional chest pain rated 10 out of 10. Which question are cardiac biomarkers ordered to answer?
opts: What is the long-term atherosclerotic risk?
That is the question a lipid profile answers. It matters for this patient eventually, but it does not tell you whether the heart is being injured right now.
How severe is any coronary stenosis?
Grading a stenosis needs imaging of the coronary arteries. A blood marker shows injury or strain to the myocardium, not the anatomy of the vessel causing it.
Which coronary artery is occluded?
No blood test localizes a lesion. Biomarkers show that myocardium is injured or stretched; the territory comes from the electrocardiogram and imaging.
Is there acute cardiac injury or stress?

Correct. Biomarkers are the acute question. The lipid panel answers a different one, the patient's long-term atherosclerotic risk, which is why it belongs to the routine physical rather than the chest-pain workup.

E.io: Measure and interpret the intervals, segments and waves of the cardiac cycle
E.q: Why is the corrected QT used rather than the raw QT interval?
opts: The QT interval changes with heart rate
Correct. Without correcting, the same heart would appear to have a different QT at different rates. The correction accounts for it.
The raw QT cannot be measured accurately on standard paper
It can be measured; the issue is that its value depends on rate.
The corrected value uses different units
Both are expressed in milliseconds, and the normal values are the same figures.
The raw QT applies only to men
Both raw and corrected values have separate figures for men and women.

E.io: Identify common abnormal cardiovascular imaging findings
E.q: Which chest radiograph findings are given as indicators of cardiac pathology?
opts: Coronary artery stenosis and the distribution of plaque
These require computed tomography angiography or catheter angiography.
Edema, effusion, cardiomegaly, cephalization and calcification

Correct, with tension physiology completing the list. Several are about the lungs rather than the heart, which is the point: the heart announces itself through what it does to everything around it. The calcification may be of the great vessels, the valves or the pericardium, and tension physiology completes the list.
Ejection fraction and regional wall motion abnormality
Both are functional measures requiring echocardiography or magnetic resonance.
Valve pressure gradients and regurgitant volume
These are Doppler measurements made on echocardiography rather than findings visible on a plain film.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 6

E.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
E.q: In what order do the five phases of the cardiac action potential occur?
opts: Phase 0, then 1, 2, 3 and 4
This reads the numbers in order, but the cycle begins at the resting state, which is phase four.
Phase 1, then 2, 3, 4 and 0
Neither the starting point nor the order matches the described sequence.
Phase 4, then 3, 2, 1 and 0
The sequence runs from phase four into phase zero and then upward, not downward.
Phase 4, then 0, 1, 2 and 3
Correct. The numbering does not run in order, which is exactly why it is worth learning as a sequence rather than as a list: rest is phase four, and the upstroke that follows it is phase zero.

E.io: Compare and contrast cardiac biomarkers: Creatine kinase, Cardiac troponins, BNP, hs-CRP
E.q: A 38-year-old has a markedly elevated C-reactive protein, far above the healthy range of less than 0.3 mg/dL. Which process typically produces the highest levels?
opts: Acute bacterial infection
Correct. Overall, the highest levels occur with bacterial infections; severe elevation above 50 mg/dL is generally seen in acute bacterial infection.
Uncomplicated obesity
Obesity causes a normal or minor elevation, in the 0.3 to 1.0 mg/dL band, not the highest levels.
Cigarette smoking
Smoking causes a mild baseline elevation, in the minor band, not a marked one.
Normal pregnancy
Pregnancy sits in the normal-or-minor elevation band, far below the levels seen with bacterial infection.

E.io: Analyze a lipid profile
E.q: A 48-year-old has triglycerides of 900 mg/dL (desirable below 150 mg/dL). Which acute risk does this level carry?
opts: Pancreatitis
Correct. Triglycerides of 500 mg/dL or above are severe hypertriglyceridemia with pancreatitis risk, and 1000 mg/dL or above is extreme.
Rhabdomyolysis
Rhabdomyolysis is skeletal muscle breakdown, evaluated with creatine kinase, and is not a recognized risk of high triglycerides.
Aortic dissection
Aortic dissection is not linked to triglyceride level; the acute risk is pancreatitis.
Pulmonary embolism
Pulmonary embolism is not the risk attached to severe hypertriglyceridemia.

E.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
E.q: A heart is being paced at a rate in the forties, with no sinoatrial activity. Which pacemaker is most likely responsible?
opts: The sinoatrial node
The sinoatrial node paces at sixty to a hundred, and the question states it is not firing.
The Purkinje network
The Purkinje network paces more slowly still, at twenty to forty.
The atrioventricular node
Correct. Its intrinsic rate is forty to sixty, and it takes over as the backup when the sinoatrial node fails.
The bundle of His alone
The bundle of His conducts rather than being described as an independent pacemaker with its own rate.

E.io: Determine heart rate using an electrocardiogram
E.q: How is the ATRIAL rate obtained by the six-second method?
opts: Count the QRS complexes and multiply by ten
That gives the ventricular rate; the atrial rate needs the P waves.
Count the P waves in six seconds and multiply by ten
Correct, and doing both counts separately is what reveals a heart block, where the two rates differ.
Count the T waves and multiply by ten
The T wave is a ventricular event and is not counted for atrial rate.
Measure the PR interval and divide into sixty
The PR interval is not used to derive a rate; P waves are counted over six seconds instead.

E.io: Describe the fundamental principles of electrocardiography
E.q: What does a BIPOLAR lead measure?
opts: The voltage difference between two distinct body points
Correct. Two real electrodes with a defined polarity, which is what separates leads I, II and III from the rest. One positive and one negative.
The electrical activity from one electrode reference point
That describes a unipolar lead, which is what the augmented and precordial leads are.
The average of all ten electrodes simultaneously
No lead is described as averaging all ten; the bipolar leads compare two points.
The mechanical movement of the chamber beneath it
Electrocardiography measures electrical activity rather than mechanical movement.

E.io: Compare and contrast cardiovascular imaging modalities
E.q: Which study is used to evaluate a patient with claudication and suspected peripheral arterial disease?
opts: Transthoracic echocardiography
It evaluates chamber size, ventricular function and valves in the heart, not the arteries of the legs affected in claudication.
Non-contrast cardiac computed tomography
It is used for coronary artery calcium scoring in the heart rather than for evaluating leg arteries in claudication or peripheral arterial disease.
Arterial vascular ultrasound
Correct. Evaluation of claudication and peripheral arterial disease is a listed indication, and it is fast, portable and free of ionizing radiation.
Electrophysiological testing
It investigates and treats cardiac rhythm disorders and says nothing about the arteries supplying the legs, which vascular ultrasound assesses.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 16

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
E.q: Which complications of exercise stress testing are described?
opts: Contrast-induced nephropathy
No contrast is given in a standard exercise stress test. The complications are arrhythmia, angina, infarction and death.
Malignancy induced by radiation exposure
The standard exercise test uses no ionizing radiation. Its complications are arrhythmia, angina, infarction and death.
Esophageal perforation
That risk belongs to transesophageal echocardiography rather than to exercise testing.
Arrhythmia, angina, infarction and death
Correct. The test deliberately provokes the thing it is looking for, which is why it is supervised and why it has a stopping rule.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 30

E.io: Describe laboratory findings associated with platelet abnormalities
E.q: A 22-year-old woman has thrombocytopenia, and her smear shows large, pale gray platelets. Which syndrome fits?
opts: May-Hegglin anomaly
May-Hegglin anomaly (a myosin heavy chain 9 disorder) shows inclusions within neutrophils, not gray platelets.
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura shows fragmented red cells (schistocytes), not gray platelets.
Spurious thrombocytopenia
Spurious thrombocytopenia shows platelet clumps and satellitism, not large gray platelets.
Gray platelet syndrome
Correct. Macrothrombocytopenia with gray platelets on the smear is gray platelet syndrome.

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
E.q: Which is a listed indication for coronary angiography?
opts: Screening an asymptomatic patient
Screening is not an indication for an invasive study carrying the risks this one does.
Suspected deep venous thrombosis
That is assessed by vascular ultrasound rather than by coronary angiography.
Newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation alone
Atrial fibrillation alone is not among the listed indications.
Severe angina despite medical therapy

Correct, together with acute infarction, a high-risk noninvasive test result, high-risk patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery, and arrhythmias suspected to be vascular in origin. Or unstable angina.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 71

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of echocardiography
E.q: What does echocardiography evaluate?
opts: The coronary artery calcium score
Calcium scoring is done by non-contrast cardiac computed tomography.
The distribution of coronary atherosclerotic plaque
Plaque distribution requires computed tomography angiography or catheter angiography.
Chamber size, ventricular function, valves, shunts and pressures

Correct. It is the functional study of the heart, which is what separates it from computed tomography, and Doppler is what adds flow and velocity to it. Wall thickness and ejection fraction come with the ventricular assessment, and Doppler adds flow and velocity.
The electrical conduction pathways of the heart
Conduction is assessed by electrocardiography and electrophysiological testing.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 20

E.io: Discuss indications for ordering cardiac biomarkers
E.q: A 60-year-old woman with rest angina has serial troponins that stay below the 99th percentile limit. What do the results indicate?
opts: A small infarction has occurred
An infarction would show troponin above the limit with a rising or falling pattern; normal serial values exclude injury.
The test is invalid in angina
Assessing unstable angina is a recognized application of troponin, so the result is interpretable.
Heart failure is excluded
Troponin addresses injury, not heart failure. A natriuretic peptide is the rule-out test for new heart failure.
No cardiac muscle injury has occurred
Correct. Normal troponins in unstable angina mean no myocyte injury. Elevated troponins would mean injury, which stratifies risk and prompts consideration of revascularization.

E.io: Analyze a lipid profile
E.q: A 57-year-old's clinician chooses to follow non-HDL-C (non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol) rather than LDL-C (low-density lipoprotein cholesterol). Why?
opts: It is measured directly by the lab
It is calculated, total cholesterol minus HDL-C (high-density lipoprotein cholesterol), not measured directly.
It excludes remnant particles
It includes remnants; that is part of why it predicts better than LDL-C alone.
It predicts risk better, at no cost
Correct. It captures cholesterol in every atherogenic apoB (apolipoprotein B) lipoprotein, adds no cost, predicts atherosclerotic risk better than LDL-C, and is recommended for routine reporting.
It has a single normal value
Like LDL-C, it has no single normal value; its goal depends on the patient's risk tier.

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
E.q: What distinguishes a pseudoaneurysm at the puncture site from a simple hematoma?
opts: It is larger but does not pulsate
Pulsatility is the distinguishing feature, along with a continuous communication with the artery.
It pulsates, and still communicates with the artery
Correct. Blood still moves in and out of it, which is why it can keep expanding and why the site is always checked.
It resolves without intervention in every case
The continuous arterial communication is what makes it more than a bruise.
It occurs only in the radial artery
The femoral site is the one specifically illustrated, and what defines it is pulsatility and arterial communication.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 78

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of stress testing
E.q: Which patients receive a pharmacological rather than an exercise stress test?
opts: Those with a normal resting electrocardiogram
A normal resting tracing makes the standard exercise test easier to interpret rather than ruling it out.
Those who cannot exercise
Correct. The heart still has to be stressed; if the legs cannot do it, a drug does it instead. Usually because of a physical limitation.
Those with renal impairment
Renal impairment is a consideration for iodinated contrast rather than for exercise capacity.
Those under forty years of age
Age is not the basis for choosing it; inability to exercise, usually from a physical limitation, is.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 38

E.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
E.q: Which property allows an impulse to spread from one myocyte to the next?
opts: Conductivity
Correct. It is what turns a single cell's discharge into a coordinated wave across the whole muscle.
Automaticity
Automaticity is the ability to generate an impulse rather than to pass one along.
Excitability
Excitability is the ability to respond to a stimulus, which is a property of the receiving cell rather than of the spread itself.
Contractility
Contractility is the mechanical response to the impulse rather than its propagation.

E.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
E.q: A 50-year-old man with sepsis has a prolonged prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time, low fibrinogen, a raised D-dimer and a low platelet count. Which diagnosis fits?
opts: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura lowers the platelet count but leaves the prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time and fibrinogen normal.
Immune thrombocytopenia
Immune thrombocytopenia lowers only the platelet count, with normal clotting times and fibrinogen.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Correct. This is the pattern of acute disseminated intravascular coagulation: prolonged screens, low fibrinogen and platelets, and a raised D-dimer.
Vitamin K antagonist effect
A vitamin K antagonist prolongs the prothrombin time alone, with a normal partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen and platelet count.

E.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
E.q: A 35-year-old woman has a low suspicion of thrombosis, and her D-dimer is below the reference limit. What does the normal result do?
opts: It confirms thrombosis
A raised D-dimer is nonspecific, so it cannot confirm thrombosis, and a normal value does the opposite, helping to exclude it.
It shows the clotting factors are normal
Factor activity is judged by prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time. D-dimer only reflects fibrin breakdown.
It measures platelet function
D-dimer measures fibrin breakdown, not platelet behavior. Platelet function has its own tests, such as aggregometry.
It helps exclude thrombosis
Correct. D-dimer is best used for its high negative predictive value: a normal result helps exclude thrombosis.

E.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
E.q: A 58-year-old man has a prolonged prothrombin time with a low platelet count. Why can one abnormal value not diagnose disseminated intravascular coagulation?
opts: The prothrombin time is always normal in it
The prothrombin time is prolonged in disseminated intravascular coagulation, not normal.
Platelet counts rise in it
The platelet count falls in it, because platelets are consumed in clots throughout the body.
Only a bleeding time can diagnose it
Bleeding time is not a diagnostic test for it, and the diagnosis rests on the pattern of the platelet count, clotting times, fibrin degradation products and inhibitors.
Other conditions can cause each abnormality
Correct. Each abnormality has other causes, for example liver failure, vitamin K deficiency and major blood loss, so the overall picture matters.

E.io: Identify the standard limb and precordial leads and their proper anatomical placement
E.q: A standard twelve-lead electrocardiogram uses how many physical electrodes?
opts: Ten
Correct. Each electrode is a different point of view, and the machine derives twelve views from the ten it is given.
Twelve
Twelve is the number of derived views rather than the number of electrodes placed.
Six
Six is the number of precordial leads rather than the total electrode count.
Fifteen
Ten electrodes are placed for a standard twelve-lead tracing.

E.io: Discuss diagnostic testing for: primary hemostasis, secondary hemostasis, fibrinolysis
E.q: A 22-year-old man has an isolated prolonged partial thromboplastin time that corrects on mixing. Which next test is indicated?
opts: A Bethesda assay
The Bethesda assay quantifies a specific factor inhibitor, relevant when the mix fails to correct.
A factor VIII assay
Correct. When a prolonged partial thromboplastin time corrects on mixing, evaluate for factor deficiency, beginning with the factor VIII assay.
A dilute Russell viper venom time
That test detects lupus anticoagulant, an inhibitor, which fails to correct on mixing.
A fibrinogen antigen
Fibrinogen antigen is measured when fibrinogen activity is low, not as the next step after correction.

E.io: Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of coronary angiography
E.q: What does catheter ablation do during electrophysiological testing?
opts: Stimulates the area to restore normal conduction
Stimulation is used to identify the arrhythmia; the ablation destroys rather than restores.
Places a permanent pacing wire in the atrium
Catheters are placed for the study, but ablation itself destroys tissue.
Delivers a drug directly to the arrhythmic focus
Ablation is a physical rather than a pharmacological treatment.
Inactivates part of the heart by destroying that tissue
Correct. The tissue is not merely silenced but destroyed, which is what makes the treatment definitive.
E.cite: Cardiac Imaging and Vascular Studies - Elwaya.pptx, Slide 62

E.io: Interpret common coagulation studies including: PT, INR, aPTT, D-dimer
E.q: A newborn has umbilical stump bleeding and lifelong severe bleeding later. The prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time and thrombin time are normal. Which deficiency fits?
opts: Factor XIII
Correct. Factor XIII deficiency gives umbilical stump bleeding and lifelong severe bleeding of any tissue with normal screening tests.
Factor VII
Factor VII deficiency prolongs the prothrombin time, which is normal in this patient.
Factor VIII
Factor VIII deficiency prolongs the partial thromboplastin time.
Factor IX
Factor IX deficiency also prolongs the partial thromboplastin time.

E.io: Discuss indications for ordering a lipid profile
E.q: A 54-year-old woman had a borderline lipoprotein(a) before menopause. When is repeating it reasonable?
opts: After starting a statin
Statins do not lower lipoprotein(a), so starting one is no reason to repeat it.
After fasting overnight
Lipoprotein(a) does not require fasting, so fasting is no reason to repeat it.
After a viral illness
Acute illness disturbs C-reactive protein, which is an acute-phase reactant; lipoprotein(a) is largely genetic.
After menopause
Correct. Although a single lifetime measurement generally suffices, repeat measurement is reasonable in women after menopause, particularly if the premenopausal level was borderline.

E.io: Describe action potentials and impulse conduction through the cardiac conduction system
E.q: Which ion entering the cell during the plateau causes contraction?
opts: Sodium
Sodium drives the upstroke in phase zero rather than the contraction, which calcium triggers.
Potassium
Potassium movement repolarizes the cell rather than triggering contraction.
Chloride
Chloride is not among the ions described in these phases; sodium, potassium and calcium are.
Calcium
Correct. It is the link between the electrical event and the mechanical one, which is why the plateau is where excitation becomes contraction.
